observation: Phase-2 architecture critique (8/10, 1 revision) caught two REAL correctness gaps before any code: (1) task-CAS proposed as bare WHERE-guard UPDATE with the audit-trail JSON read-modify-write OUTSIDE the CAS atomicity — clobbers audit entries under a 3-way race; fix = wrap SELECT-validate+audit-read+CAS-UPDATE in db.transaction in BOTH kernel and fabric copies, emit post-commit. (2) async propagation handlers (void async IIFE) run on microtask queue AFTER /kill returns, so AC6 asserting the async skip row would flake AND two rows exist per task-kill (sync cascade 'applied' + async upward 'skipped'); fix = disambiguate by sourceEvent and assert AC6 on the deterministic sync rows. Both hard-to-debug-at-runtime, folded into plan in one tight loop.

Code review verdict DONE first pass, zero blocking findings. Reviewer carried Phase-2 critique context forward and re-verified every Phase-2 contract in the diff (transaction mirror is a true structural mirror not a weaker WHERE-only guard; cascade propagation insert verified field-for-field against logPropagation; phantom-row guard present; session terminal write emits no session_ended). Two-review model confirmed comprehensive. 31 AF12 tests green, full green phase 4088 pass.

Long green phase: test commit 18:28 → feat green 19:05 ≈ 37 min wall (~2.2M ms builder time), the single largest time block of the run. No rework inside it (DONE first pass) so the time was productive, not churn. Total run ~80 min, 10 commits, sequential phases.

A single money-contract sweep at green time, or treating O1 as in-scope before DONE, would have saved a commit/push round-trip.
